title: Custom subgraph resolvers are unguarded by default and must enforce authorization themselves
content:
## The gap

`ph generate subgraph --name <name>` scaffolds resolvers that call the reactor **directly, with no permission check**. Nothing in the generated code consults the authorization service.

The leak is twofold: the resolver returns document contents the caller may not be entitled to, and — because a missing document and a forbidden document are indistinguishable in the response — it also leaks the *existence* of protected documents.

## What to do instead

Use the enforcement helpers `BaseSubgraph` exposes: `assertCanRead`, `assertCanWrite`, `assertCanExecuteOperation`, `assertCanCreate` (all throw Forbidden), plus the non-throwing `canReadDocument` for filtering lists.

Always re-fetch through `AuthorizedDocumentHandle.fetchIdentifier` rather than the caller's raw identifier — permission rows key on canonical ids, so reusing a caller-supplied slug after an assert lets an attacker alias one document's slug onto another.
